channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) has published a clinical practice guideline using the GRADE approach for rehabilitating athletes with hamstring strain injury, providing evidence-based guidance for physical therapists.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Somatosensory Interventions on Sensory, Motor, and Balance Functions in Individuals with Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (330 participants) found that somatosensory interventions significantly improved Berg Balance Scale scores in stroke patients compared to conventional therapy, but no significant pooled effects were observed for upper limb motor function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis (13 trials) found that very low-certainty evidence shows percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) added to therapeutic exercise (TE) is not superior to sham plus TE or TE alone for pain or function in tendinopathies. Low-certainty evidence suggests PNE plus TE may offer greater short- and medium-term pain reduction compared with dry needling (DN) plus TE in tendinopathies, but not in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Optimal exercise dose in adults with chronic low back pain disorders: systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis of 239 trials found that low-to-moderate exercise doses were associated with short-term clinically meaningful improvements in disability and pain intensity for chronic low back pain, with limited additional benefit at higher exposure. Optimal doses were predicted as 4 sessions/week, 25 min/session over 13 weeks for disability, and 3 sessions/week, 30 min/session over 8 weeks for pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence on whether reduced spinal range of motion is a prognostic factor for pain intensity, disability, and global recovery in people with specific or nonspecific spinal pain, with most studies reporting no clear association and high risk of bias.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Mirror therapy versus functional electrical stimulation cycling in post-stroke lower limb rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=45) found that both mirror therapy (MD -2.60, 95% CI -5.83 to -0.63, p=0.004) and functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling (MD -3.00, 95% CI -6.23 to -0.23, p=0.008) improved lower extremity motor function more than conventional rehabilitation in subacute stroke patients, with no significant difference between the two adjunct therapies.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review of six studies (173 ACLR participants, 79 controls) found shear wave elastography (SWE) detects muscle-specific mechanical deficits after ACLR, with reduced passive vastus medialis shear modulus (g -1.10 to -1.21) and semitendinosus stiffness (g -1.29 to -1.64) after hamstring harvest.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: This paper outlines a staged return-to-performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, comprising structured on-field rehabilitation, return to team training, return to competitive match play, and sustained performance, underpinned by four interdependent pillars: movement quality, technical/tactical re-training, physical reconditioning, and neuromuscular performance restoration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Identifying heterogeneous patterns of real-world upper limb use beyond motor severity: a cross-sectional sensor-based study in people with subacute stroke
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 101 subacute stroke patients used accelerometers and FMA-UL to identify six heterogeneous upper limb activity patterns, distinguishing between motor deficits, learned non-use, and UL inattention. Clinical variables like ARAT, MAL, and UL inattention were key differentiators.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: The effects of route previewing on adaptive gait and gaze behaviour under cognitive dual-task conditions in older adults
item.description: A study (n=39 older adults) found that route previewing before gait initiation attenuates the negative effects of cognitive load on adaptive gait, reducing stepping errors and cross-steps (p < .001) and improving gaze efficiency, likely by supporting visual motor planning.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Transitions and predictive factors of cognitive frailty states in rural older adults: a prospective cohort study
item.description: A prospective cohort study of 3,243 rural older adults from China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study found cognitive frailty (CF) to be reversible, with the intensity of recovery from reversible CF (RCF) to only non-dementia cognitive impairment (NDCI) being 0.429 (95% CI 0.359–0.512), highlighting early RCF as a key intervention window.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Calf Injuries: An Anatomy-Based Approach to Diagnosis, Management and Return to Sport.
item.description: A review of calf muscle injuries highlights the heterogeneity of lesions and emphasizes an anatomy-based approach to diagnosis and management, moving beyond muscle-based classifications. It supports criteria-based, progressive loading rehabilitation and multifactorial return-to-sport decisions, noting limited evidence linking specific anatomical patterns to prognosis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Validity and Reliability of Accelerometers to Evaluate Preschool-Aged Children’s Physical Activity and Sedentary Behavior During Free-Living Condition: A Systematic Review
item.description: A systematic review found accelerometers to be valid and reliable for assessing physical activity in preschool-aged children in free-living conditions, but less reliable for sedentary behavior, with no clear pooled direction.
item.author: Meas Phys Educ Exerc Sci

item.title: Effects of Using High-Frequency TENS During an Exercise Therapy Program in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
item.description: This sham-controlled RCT found that adding high-frequency transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation to an exercise therapy program did not provide additional benefits for pain or function in 96 individuals with knee osteoarthritis (adjusted mean difference, 1.05 points; 95% CI, -5.19 to 7.29 for KOOS Pain subscale post-intervention).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical therapy care utilization and associated sociodemographic and clinical factors among noncommunicable diseases in the brazilian population: A cross-sectional, population-based study.
item.description: A cross-sectional study using the 2019 National Health Survey database (n=88,531 Brazilians with NCDs) found that stroke survivors had the highest physical therapy utilization (17.0%; 95% CI: 15.4%, 18.7%). Follow-up by a healthcare professional was a common associated factor across stroke, chronic back pain, and chronic respiratory diseases.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of cluster-set vs. traditional resistance exercise with equated total rest on muscular performance, perceived fatigue, and cardiovascular responses in resistance-trained women
item.description: A crossover RCT with 12 resistance-trained women found that cluster-set configurations (10-s and 30-s intra-set rest) significantly improved muscular endurance (18.4 ± 1.7 reps for CLS30 vs. 12.8 ± 1.2 for TRS) and reduced perceived fatigue compared to traditional sets, with equated total rest.
item.author: Sport Sci Health

item.title: "It's not for me": community-based fall prevention exercise programs for those aging into disability.
item.description: A qualitative study (n=11) explored barriers for adults aged 50+ with self-reported mobility, vision, or hearing impairment participating in community-based fall prevention exercise programs. Themes included lack of awareness/access, interconnected barriers, disability experiences, and program design challenges, revealing that participants often don't identify with programs due to stigma and misalignment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Identifying Indicators of Advanced Levels of Clinical Competence in Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy: A Francophone Delphi Study
item.description: A Francophone Delphi study (n=27 experts) identified 13 indicators of advanced clinical competence in musculoskeletal physiotherapy, with 10 achieving consensus on formulation. These indicators primarily reflected advanced clinical reasoning, such as real-time adaptation and decision-making under uncertainty, rather than standardized outcome attainment.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Immediate effects of suspension walker support on locomotor behavior of pre-walking infants with Down syndrome
item.description: A study on pre-walking infants with Down syndrome (DS) (ages 10-19 months) found that suspension walkers robustly increased locomotor behavior, including upright time and stepping rate. Most walker movement was caregiver-initiated, and infants stepped more while the walker was moving.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: The effects of blood flow restriction training on lower limb motor function and balance in stroke patients: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A 3-week regimen of blood flow restriction (BFR) walking or low-load BFR resistance training significantly improved lower limb motor function and balance in 96 stroke patients compared to conventional training, with 34.4% of LL-BFR participants achieving MCID for FMA-LE vs 15.6% in control.
item.author: PubMed
